rites.name: Brestar
rites.text: Brestar is the concept of the first sounding in Osyuseth, the note that gathers the roots of the world out of silence during the Singing. It is less a being than a pressure that makes matter agree to hold together.

rites.name: Thyustasora
rites.text: Thyustasora is the concept of Osyuseth's first sounding, the pitch that drew loose matter together into the first roots of the world during the Singing. It is less a thing than a tone that still hangs in the structure of the realm, measured by what it can bind rather than what it can break.

rites.name: Bruldareld
rites.text: Bruldareld is the concept of Osyuseth's sounding in the Singing, the undated tone by which the first roots of the world condense into being. Among the temples and orders of the Holy Age, it is remembered as the moment flame first learned to hold its shape.

rites.name: Thouthak
rites.text: Thouthak is the concept of the threshold-keeping that Osyuseth's Courts gave to the doors between worlds, a principle of measured passage rather than a single being. In the Courts of the second Era it was the rule that weighed who might cross and at what cost, and its authority was felt at the scale of whole realms.

rites.name: Serirnellum
rites.text: Serirnellum is the concept of a slow hush that settled over Osyuseth during the Fall, when the old lattice of worlds began to fray. It is remembered as the quiet that followed the Sundering, the stillness in which the Shards drifted apart and the Pact was first sworn.

rites.name: Silium
rites.text: Silium is the concept of the living pact that bound the broken worlds of Osyuseth after the Sundering, a quiet tie that let groves and young kingdoms take root in the shards. It is remembered as the first promise made between separated lands, and every oath sworn beneath the Age of the first sovereign was measured against it.

rites.name: Coralaurnus
rites.text: Coralaurnus is a concept of Osyuseth born in the Fall, when worlds split and the first sovereign swore the Pact among the broken Shards. It names the living coral-groves that grew over the drifting fragments and bound the growing kingdoms to one another in the Age that followed.

rites.name: Manor
rites.text: A bodily technique in which a hunter drives fluid pressure through its limbs to launch a sudden, explosive leap. Only one swift stalker kind is able to perform it.

rites.name: Sileriolora
rites.text: Sileriolora is the concept of a quiet, hushed gap that the orders of Osyuseth learned to name during the Walled Age, when holding walls and first crossings were built around it. In the Holy Age its temples kept lamps burning to mark where the gap was thinnest. It is understood as a kind of stillness that waits between one thing and the next.

rites.name: Amestium Cestium
rites.text: A dose introduced into the body that dulls the sense of dread, letting a person hold firm before a monstrous hunter so it hesitates or withdraws. Its making traces back to an army surgeon who helped shape it.

rites.name: Loliranum
rites.text: A silent tongue of the open hand, in which shaped gestures and sweeping motions carry meaning between speakers. It was once shared widely by peoples who could not rely on sound alone.

rites.name: Isethith
rites.text: Isethith is a mind-weaving discipline in the Osyuseth cosmos, where practitioners graft a stranger's thoughts into a crystal lattice of starlight to steady drifting worlds. Its adepts are known for rebuilding failing suns by tuning remembered sensations into gravitational harmonics. The art is feared for its cost, since each imprint leaves a lingering echo in the mind that refuses to fade.

rites.name: Oraulor
rites.text: A lethal strike in which a hunter drives its inner jaw through a victim's skull, punching clean through to the other side. It can defeat even armored head coverings.

rites.name: Nernum Oraulium
rites.text: A method that halts the flow of time around a sleeping body, usually a living traveler. It is mostly used to cross vast distances between distant worlds.

rites.name: Eliorinna
rites.text: Eliorinna is a concept in Osyuseth that holds the branching of the Three Futures, where each possible ending is shelved in the Library for later reading. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between peoples, it was said to whisper which branch was thinnest.
